headline: Revenue slips on U.S. headwinds, cost cuts swing to profit
summary_short: Inspire Medical's Q2 2026 revenue fell 7.6% y/y to $200.6M on U.S. coding/reimbursement headwinds, but lower opex swung the company to $0.3M net income (diluted EPS $0.01) from a $3.6M loss a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue fell 7.6% y/y to $200.6M on U.S. coding/reimbursement headwinds, partly offset by International growth; gross margin still expanded 150bps to 85.5% on mix shift toward Inspire V, so gross profit dollars fell only 6.0% y/y to $171.5M. Opex fell 7.4% to $172.0M (lower stock comp, lower marketing), narrowing the operating loss to $0.5M from $3.3M. Net income swung to $0.3M (diluted EPS $0.01) from a $3.6M loss, aided by a smaller other-expense line (prior year had a $4.0M impairment) despite an 89.9% tax rate. Operating cash flow was $23.2M vs $2.7M; cash rose 19.5% y/y to $127.8M and equity grew 21.8% to $825.6M. FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $835-875M; new 'Project Horizon' plan targets ~$30M of annualized reinvestment capacity.

drivers.explanation: Decline driven primarily by lower U.S. revenue tied to the evolving coding and reimbursement environment, partially offset by growth in International revenue.
Dollar gross profit fell only because revenue declined faster than cost of goods sold; gross margin itself rose 150bps to 85.5% on a higher-margin mix shift toward the Inspire V system.
Operating expenses fell $13.8M (-7.4%) to $172.0M, driven by lower stock-based compensation (elevated a year ago by accelerated vesting) and lower marketing expense.

Improved operating result plus a smaller other-expense line (prior year included a $4.0M impairment charge) drove the swing to profit, despite a higher 89.9% effective tax rate from stock-comp tax shortfalls.
Tracks net income's swing to a $0.3M profit from a $3.6M loss a year earlier, on a roughly flat diluted share count.
Operating cash flow was $23.2M this quarter versus $2.7M a year earlier, driven by improved working capital in receivables and inventories.
Not explained in the release for this specific quarter; no equity-roll-forward commentary was given beyond the balance sheet.

Revenue fell 7.6% y/y on U.S. coding/reimbursement headwinds, but opex discipline and mix shift drove a swing to slight GAAP profitability; the company also raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $835-875M and launched 'Project Horizon,' a restructuring plan targeting ~$30M of annualized reinvestment capacity.
